discovery: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms and its use for precision measurement of inertia, gravity and fundamental constants

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Université Sorbonne Paris Nord / SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Bordé showed that laser-driven atomic transitions act as coherent beam splitters, making the Ramsey spectrometer an atom interferometer. Pritchard realised the first interferometer for atoms with material gratings and used it for precise measurements of atomic properties. Kasevich, with Chu, invented the light-pulse atom interferometer using stimulated Raman transitions. He then turned it into instruments of extraordinary sensitivity: gravimeters, gradiometers and gyroscopes, and meter-scale fountains that probe the equivalence principle and show gravitationally induced quantum phases. Atom interferometers now give the best determinations of the fine-structure constant, measure Newton's G, test general relativity with quantum matter, and are being deployed for geodesy, navigation and future gravitational-wave and dark-matter searches. This work has made the wave nature of massive particles a practical and field-deployable tool, bringing quantum mechanics and gravity together in the laboratory with the same metrological rigour that underpins atomic clocks.
